title: Rubinstein's Immortal
summary: Rubinstein's Immortal is remembered for a short, sharp sacrifice sequence in which Black gives up a rook to open White's king and then finishes with a bishop check and a mating net. The evaluation barely moves for 30 plies, so the lesson is in the slow buildup and in White's 19.e5 blunder, which handed Black a winning attack. Watch how Black's rooks and bishops are aimed at the king on h1 long before the sacrifices begin.

moves.comment: 1.d4 opens the queen's pawn game. The engine slightly prefers 1.e4, but d4 is perfectly sound and keeps the centre flexible.
1...d5 mirrors White's pawn and contests the centre directly. It is a solid, classical reply.
2.Nf3 develops a knight and prepares to castle, bringing pressure to bear on the centre.
2...e6 builds a firm pawn chain that supports d5. The engine rates it as the best move.
3.e3 is solid but slightly passive. The engine prefers 3.c4 at once to claim the centre.
3...c5 strikes at the centre immediately, challenging the d4 pawn. The engine prefers the calmer 3...Nf6.
4.c4 reinforces d4 and fixes the pawn structure. The engine prefers 4.Be2, though the position stays level.
4...Nc6 develops a knight and adds pressure on d4. The engine rates it as the best move.
5.Nc3 develops and adds a defender to the centre. The engine prefers 5.cxd5 instead.
5...Nf6 completes the knight development and prepares to castle. The engine rates it as the best move.
6.dxc5 captures a pawn and opens the d-file. The engine prefers 6.cxd5, and the evaluation eases slightly towards equality.
6...Bxc5 recaptures with the bishop, developing it actively. The engine rates it as the best move and the position is level.
7.a3 stops ...Bb4 and prepares b4 to gain queenside space. The engine rates it as the best move.
7...a6 prevents a later b5 by White and keeps options open. The engine prefers castling first with 7...O-O.
8.b4 gains space and tries to chase the bishop away. The engine rates it as the best move.
8...Bd6 retreats the bishop. The engine prefers 8...Ba7, keeping the long diagonal.
9.Bb2 develops the bishop onto a long diagonal aimed at the centre. The engine prefers the immediate 9.cxd5.
9...O-O castles, securing the king and connecting the rooks. The engine rates it as the best move.
10.Qd2 develops the queen and prepares further piece play. The engine prefers 10.cxd5.
10...Qe7 supports the centre and prepares rook play on the d-file. The engine rates it as the best move.
11.Bd3 retreats the bishop and allows ...dxc4 with the initiative. The engine prefers 11.cxd5, and the evaluation swings to Black's favour.

moment.title: Bishop retreat hands over the initiative
moment.text: 11.Bd3 looks natural, but it lets Black capture on c4 with the d-file open. The engine prefers 11.cxd5, and the evaluation moves from +0.3 to -0.6. Notice how a single tempo decides who controls the centre.

moves.comment: 11...dxc4 captures the pawn and opens the d-file for Black's rook. The engine rates it as the best move.
12.Bxc4 regains the pawn and keeps the position balanced. The engine rates it as the best move.
12...b5 attacks the bishop with a pawn and gains queenside space. The engine rates it as the best move.
13.Bd3 retreats the bishop again, keeping it active on the d-file. The engine rates it as the best move.
13...Rd8 places the rook on the open d-file. The engine prefers 13...Bb7 with the bishop developed first.
14.Qe2 moves the queen to a flexible square. The engine prefers 14.O-O to castle first.
14...Bb7 develops the bishop to the long diagonal aimed at White's kingside. The engine rates it as the best move.
15.O-O castles, connecting the rooks. The engine rates it as the best move.
15...Ne5 centralises the knight and offers an exchange. The engine rates it as the best move.
16.Nxe5 accepts the exchange and simplifies the position. The engine rates it as the best move.
16...Bxe5 recaptures and centralises the bishop. The engine rates it as the best move.
17.f4 gains space and prepares e4, but it weakens the king's position. The engine prefers 17.Rfd1 and the evaluation drops to -1.1.

moment.title: 17.f4 weakens the king
moment.text: Pushing the f-pawn gains space but removes a shelter pawn from the White king. The engine prefers 17.Rfd1, and the evaluation falls from -0.3 to -1.1. Black's bishop then settles on c7 with a long-term grip on the kingside.

moves.comment: 17...Bc7 keeps the bishop on a useful diagonal toward the kingside. The engine rates it as the best move.
18.e4 advances the centre, but the evaluation slides further. The engine prefers 18.Rad1.
18...Rac8 doubles rooks on the c-file to pressure c3. The engine prefers 18...Nh5, though the move is still good.
19.e5 is a blunder that closes the diagonal and lets Black's bishop swing in with check. The evaluation jumps to -5.3 and the attack becomes decisive. The engine prefers 19.Kh1.

moment.title: 19.e5 is the decisive error
moment.text: Closing the centre with e5 blocks White's own bishop and allows ...Bb6+ with tempo. The evaluation jumps from -2.1 to -5.3, the engine's clearest turning point. Black's bishop check opens the diagonal to the king on h1.

moves.comment: 19...Bb6+ checks the king along the long diagonal, forcing White to respond. The engine rates it as the best move.
20.Kh1 is the only sensible way to escape the check. The engine rates it as the best move.
20...Ng4 brings the knight into the attack against the kingside. The engine rates it as the best move.
21.Be4 blocks the e-file and tries to hold the position together. The engine rates it as the best move.
21...Qh4 attacks the h-pawn and joins the assault. The engine prefers 21...Nxh2, though the queen move is still good.
22.g3 kicks the queen but opens lines towards White's own king. The engine rates it as the best move, yet the evaluation sinks to -8.3.
22...Rxc3 wins a knight with the rook and leaves White without defence. The engine rates it as the best move.

moment.title: 22...Rxc3 cashes in the attack
moment.text: Black's rook takes the knight on c3, having been brought to the c-file earlier. The evaluation reaches -8.3 and White has no reliable way to meet the threats. The move shows how a quiet build-up turns into material gain.

moves.comment: 23.gxh4 recaptures the queen, but the evaluation becomes mate in ten for Black. The engine prefers 23.Bxb7.
23...Rd2 sacrifices the rook to deflect White's queen. The engine rates it as the best move and the mate is now nine moves away.

moment.title: 23...Rd2 sacrifice deflects the queen
moment.text: The rook gives itself up on d2 to pull the White queen away from the defence of the king. The engine now reads mate in nine for Black. Watch how the sacrifice clears the way for the bishop.

moves.comment: 24.Qxd2 accepts the rook, opening the path for Black's bishop. The engine prefers 24.Rf2, but mate is still close.
24...Bxe4+ checks the king on the long diagonal after the queen has left the defence. The engine rates it as the best move and mate is four moves away.
25.Qg2 blocks the check, the only queen move that keeps material on the board. The engine prefers 25.Rf3, but White remains lost.
25...Rh3 brings the rook to the h-file to finish the attack. The engine shows mate in three for Black and White resigned.

moment.title: 25...Rh3 leaves White without defence
moment.text: After the bishop check and the queen move, Black's rook joins the attack on the h-file. The engine shows mate in three, so the outcome is no longer in doubt. White resigned soon after.

lessons: Before pushing a pawn towards the king, check whether it removes a defender or closes your own piece's diagonal.
When retreating a bishop, consider whether a capture with tempo or an opened file gives your opponent the initiative.
Keep your rooks and bishops aimed at the enemy king, because quiet pieces often become the source of a sudden sacrifice.
